target_problem: polynomial evaluation of the V92 canonical child-count sign for NC0_3-Avoid[n,n+1], as a possible route to improving the Huang-Li-Zhong O(n*2^(n/2)) all-instance baseline
conditional_implication: If exact child comparison N(p0)<=N(p1) were polynomial-time for every arbitrary prefix of the fixed V94 arity-at-most-three language at stretch one, then P=PP. V94 proves this arbitrary-prefix barrier. It does not extend the implication to V92-generated canonical prefixes or to comparison-free range avoidance.
frontier_reason: The result closes an overstrong evaluator subgoal and isolates the canonical-prefix/comparison-free gap; it does not improve the all-instance avoidance runtime or trigger a circuit-lower-bound transfer theorem.

current_gap: The explicit PP-hard prefix is noncanonical at its first balanced DEF gate. The remaining algorithmic question is whether canonical prefixes escape this comparison hardness or whether avoidance can bypass exact comparison entirely.
result_obtained: A fixed-language PP-completeness theorem for arbitrary-prefix child comparison at exact stretch one, an explicit theorem separating that reduction from V92 canonical prefixes, and a polynomial exact affine comparator with a deterministic canonical avoider.
closed_route: polynomial exact child comparison for every arbitrary prefix as the generic replacement for the Huang-Li-Zhong evaluator
surviving_route: canonical-prefix structure or comparison-free avoidance, with the affine language as a tractable control
stop_rule: Do not spend further laboratories seeking a polynomial exact comparator for all arbitrary prefixes of unrestricted fixed ternary languages. V95 must either canonicalize a hardness/tractability theorem or construct avoidance from weaker information than exact comparison.
